This event consisted of four laps of three miles each and 24 teams were entered. At the end of the first lap G. Flanagan was 3rd in 18m. 13s. handing over to R.
Carr, we finished 14th out of 36 teams who closed in. G. Flanagan made a fine effort to finish 13th and would have done better but for a fall at the start of the race.
Need anymore be said except thanks to the four who did try. Two good placings in the Youths Event, with G.
Of the 17 competing teams, our "A" team finished 6th and our "B" Team 9th. Outstanding lap times were G.Flanagan 9.34 and A.Mole 9.43.

Chas Walker, unpredictable as ever, was 6th just in front of junior George Flanagan whose forward running was a surprise to many. Eric Gebbett was a deserving winner of the handicap with Ron Mitchell and Dave Hooper 2nd and 3rd respectively.
Twelve juniors lined up for the contest for the Savage Shield held at Wimbledon on 17th December. There were no surprises and G. Flanagan proved a worthy winner in 29mins. 9secs. followed by C.
Tupper dropped out dwe to stomach trouble. Positions :- 20, G.

George Flanagan was soon prominent and ran an extremely good race throughout to come through from fifth at the halfway stage to second, only eleven seconds behind the winner Bill Bird of Ranelagh who is a second claim Belgrave member.
George Flanagan performed extremely well to win the individual title and thus follows in the footsteps of Harry Shields, Ted Stimpson and Derek Burfitt, all past winners of this race.

George Flanagan was the only one of our runners who excelled himself and he should be pleased with thirteenth position. John Moore, by finishing 52nd, gained good experience in a large field and Robin Weate, in his first year with us, showed that he is possessed of more than his fair share of pluck to finish 88th.
